gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a maker's cold-weather battery limits. Lectric and Aventon say to charge only between 32°F and 104°F, and Himiway says to warm a cold pack for 2–3 hours before charging and to expect 30–50% less range below 32°F. So a battery left in a truck or hunting camp on a frosty November night can't safely be recharged until it warms up, and the ride to the stand gets a cold-shrunk battery.
standout_why: I compared against bicyclingland.com (cited), sledgeback.com, electricbikeexplorer.com and fieldandstream.com. Bicyclingland says 'We found no maker or reviewer figure for range in the cold' and only tells readers to 'check your manual's charging temperature range'. It gives no number. Sledgeback says only that 'cold reduces usable capacity significantly', with no limit. Electricbikeexplorer lists cold as one range factor, with no figure. Field & Stream mentions fall temperatures but gives no limit. Every rival says cold matters, but none gives a maker's charging floor, riding floor or warm-up time. I could not open the cited Aventon and Velotric product pages (HTTP 429), so I can't confirm those two pages leave it out.
decides: This doesn't choose between the hub-motor picks: Lectric, Aventon and Himiway's winter guide all set the same 32°F (0°C) charging floor. What it changes is how to read the range numbers. ChatGPT's 15–30 mile loaded estimate is a warm-weather figure. OutdoorGearLab measured 24.6 miles on an XPeak 2.0 at full assist plus throttle. Applying Aventon's 20% planning loss at 32°F gives about 19.7 miles (24.6 × 0.8), and Himiway's 30–50% figure gives about 12–17 miles, before any gear load. For a cold-morning hunter that favors the bigger battery or a spare pack, and keeping the battery indoors overnight. On noise, OutdoorGearLab found the XPeak 2.0's 'Stealth M24' motor was not noticeably quieter than other bikes in its test, despite Lectric's '400% quieter' claim. Quietness can't be the tiebreaker among these hub bikes.

findings.label: Charging ambient temperature window
findings.source_title: Essential eBike Battery Safety Tips | Lectric eBikes
findings.note: Lectric's wording: 'Only charge your battery when the ambient temperature is between 32°F (0°C) and 104°F (40°C).' The guide covers all Lectric batteries and does not name the XPeak 2.0.

findings.label: Riding (discharge) ambient temperature window
findings.source_title: Essential eBike Battery Safety Tips | Lectric eBikes
findings.note: Lectric's wording: 'only use your battery when the ambient temperature is between -4°F (-20°C) and 113°F (45°C).' This is generic Lectric guidance, not specific to one model.

findings.label: Charging temperature window and cold-range planning loss
findings.value: Charge between 32°F and 104°F; plan for 20% capacity loss at 32°F (0°C) and 30% at 14°F (-10°C)
findings.source_title: Loaded Aventure Range in Cold Weather: A 4-Day Planning Guide | Aventon
findings.note: Aventon blog dated 2026-11-11. The 20%/30% figures are the guide's planning assumptions, drawn from BatteryIQ and NASA 18650 cell tests (78.8% and 70.5% of 25°C capacity at -10°C). They are not measured on an Aventure. The guide says Aventon 'publishes no minimum riding temperature' and that no independent Aventure review reports a cold-weather run. Aventon's advice: 'If you park your ebike outside overnight, bring your battery inside with you.'

findings.label: Winter charging floor, riding floor and cold range loss
findings.value: Never charge below 32°F (0°C); ride down to 14°F (-10°C); expect 30–50% range loss below 32°F; warm the battery 2–3 hours at room temperature before charging
findings.source_title: E-bike Battery Care During Winter: Everything You Need to Know - Himiway eBike
findings.note: Himiway blog dated 2025-11-13, written for all Himiway bikes. It also lists a 'risk of BMS shutting down to protect cells' below 0°F (-18°C). It conflicts with Himiway's D5 2.0 battery care guide (next finding).

findings.label: Model-specific charging window (conflicts with Himiway's winter blog)
findings.source_title: Himiway D5 2.0 Battery Charging & Maintenance Ultimate Guide
findings.note: Page dated 2026-07-24. Its 14°F floor is 18°F lower than the 32°F 'never charge below' rule in Himiway's own winter blog. If we print one, the stricter 32°F figure is the safe one.

findings.label: Motor noise and measured range (independent test)
findings.value: Stealth M24 'isn't noticeably quieter than other bikes in our test'; 24.6 mi and 1,541 ft of climbing to an empty battery at PAS 5 plus throttle
findings.note: Joshua Hutchens, OutdoorGearLab, review dated 2025-03-12. No decibel measurement, no test temperature, and no rider weight for the range run. The '400% quieter' claim is Lectric's and compares against Lectric's earlier hub motors. My arithmetic: 24.6 × 0.8 = 19.7 mi using Aventon's 20% planning loss at 32°F, or 24.6 × 0.5–0.7 = 12.3–17.2 mi using Himiway's 30–50%.

unsourced: Velotric Nomad 2 charging and riding temperature limits: I looked for them in Velotric support-site PDFs and two Velotric battery blogs. A search snippet attributes 'won't charge … below 32°F (0°C); let the battery adjust to room temperature for at least 1 hour' to the Nomad 2X manual, but the PDFs wouldn't extract and the blog pages loaded truncated, so I couldn't verify it on the page.

XPeak 2.0 and Aventure 3 owner's-manual temperature specs: I couldn't find model-specific manuals. Lectric's figures above come from its brand-wide safety guide. An older Aventure (first-generation) manual reportedly gives a 50–77°F charging range, which I didn't open.
Measured motor noise in dB for any candidate: none of the reviews I found (OutdoorGearLab, plus the reviews listed in search results) used a sound meter.
Current prices from the Lectric, Aventon and Velotric product pages: each returned HTTP 429 on every try, and price wasn't this angle's job.
